restatements.text: Bans demonstrations within 100 feet of the entrance to a house of worship during scheduled services.

findings.quote: No person may demonstrate within 100 feet of the entrance of a house of worship during scheduled religious services.
findings.mechanism: Banning demonstrations near houses of worship during scheduled services restricts the times and places where people can engage in expressive demonstration.

findings.quote: No person may demonstrate within 100 feet of the entrance of a house of worship during scheduled religious services.
findings.mechanism: Establishing a buffer zone around houses of worship during scheduled services protects religious congregants from disruption and interference while engaging in religious exercise.

analysis.answer: Under current law, demonstrations are permitted on public sidewalks subject to general traffic and noise rules. The measure creates a specific restriction prohibiting demonstrations within 100 feet of the entrance to any house of worship while scheduled religious services are taking place.

Congregants attending religious services benefit from reduced noise and disruption near their venues. Individuals and groups wishing to protest at or near a house of worship bear the cost of having to move their demonstrations further away or hold them at different times.

Demonstrators are likely to relocate their activities just outside the 100-foot boundary or adjust their timing to occur before or after scheduled services. Law enforcement agencies will need to ascertain the boundaries of these buffer zones and verify the schedules of religious services to enforce the restriction.

The measure addresses the disruption of religious worship caused by nearby protests. The 100-foot buffer mechanism provides physical separation that reaches the problem of disruption, though it does so by restricting the locations where individuals can exercise free speech.

flags.quote: No person may demonstrate within 100 feet of the entrance of a house of worship during scheduled religious services.
flags.note: The measure lacks a severability clause, meaning that if the demonstration restriction is struck down by a court, the entire measure would fall.

items.text: A protected 100-foot buffer zone around houses of worship to prevent disruptions during scheduled religious services.
The freedom to demonstrate within 100 feet of a house of worship's entrance while scheduled services are occurring.
The ability to demonstrate on public spaces near houses of worship during religious services, subject only to general noise and traffic rules.
Mandatory buffer zones that shield congregants from demonstrations outside their houses of worship during scheduled services.
